classification.summary: DVM.init() is external with no initializer guard and no access control, so inside a flashLoan callback the attacker re-pointed _BASE_TOKEN_/_QUOTE_TOKEN_ at worthless tokens they controlled, making the flash-loan repayment check pass against the fake balances while the pool's real wCRES and USDT walked out.

sources.note: onchain review: I read the verified DVM source at 0x051ebd71 - init() is a plain external function with no guard. The attack tx moves 1,139,456.204397 USDT and 133,548.94 wCRES out of this pool against fake-token inflows; lossUsd is set to the USDT leg only (USD-pegged 1:1, directly verified) rather than the $2m-$3.8m headline that aggregates several pools and unconverted wCRES. Pool created 2021-02-26 by 0x96627558c67e7cf488d8fa9f359daefb43c7e834, not by attack sender 0x368a6558 Recheck of the deployment basis (DELEGATECALL audit): the victim is an EIP-1167 minimal-proxy clone: its 45-byte runtime is 363d3d373d3d3d363d73 followed by the master 0x2bbd66fc4898242bdbd2583bbe1d76e8b8f71445, so the DELEGATECALL target is baked into the code and cannot be repointed; the master's runtime is byte-identical at the clone's creation block 11932747 and the incident block 12000165 and contains no DELEGATECALL of its own, so the deployment basis is exact.
